subject.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 custom openai-completions proxy emits malformed DSML / nested arguments; tools not executed

question: Should OpenClaw treat a missing `>` in an otherwise closed DeepSeek DSML tool wrapper as recoverable tool intent, and if so what minimum grammar prevents accidental tool execution from assistant text?
rationale: The issue is a bug in a supported completions transport, but broadening recovery changes when model output becomes executable tool input and cannot be safely chosen from one proxy trace alone.

options.title: Conservative malformed-wrapper recovery
options.body: Accept the observed missing-`>` form only when the closing DSML structure, tool name, decoded object arguments, and existing tool schema validation all succeed.

options.title: Keep strict DSML framing
options.body: Recover only syntactically complete DSML and leave malformed wrapper text visible while the proxy/model behavior is corrected upstream.

options.title: Provider-specific opt-in
options.body: Add recovery only behind an owner-approved DeepSeek-compatible transport rule if the proxy variant proves too ambiguous for the shared parser.

recommendation.title: Conservative malformed-wrapper recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the observed missing-`>` form only when the closing DSML structure, tool name, decoded object arguments, and existing tool schema validation all succeed.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior merged DSML recovery on this exact transport makes this the strongest available history-based routing candidate.
